title: Exceptions Versus Ordinary Return Values
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of exceptions versus ordinary return values in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply exceptions versus ordinary return values in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to avoiding exceptions for normal branching and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Exceptions Versus Ordinary Return Values through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding exceptions versus ordinary return values helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Exceptions Versus Ordinary Return Values helps you reason about recoverable and unrecoverable conditions. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Recoverable and unrecoverable conditions. Then connect it to Result-oriented interfaces. The remaining syllabus points—Avoiding exceptions for normal branching—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Exceptions Versus Ordinary Return Values
content_blocks.code:
begin
  Integer("12x")
rescue ArgumentError
  puts "Please enter a whole number."
end

items.title: Assuming the happy path is enough
items.text: Test an empty value, a boundary value, and one invalid value before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Treating an example as a universal rule
items.text: Check Ruby version, runtime implementation, and third-party library documentation when behavior is version-sensitive.

items.title: Mixing too many concerns
items.text: Separate input parsing, domain behavior, and output so each piece is easier to test.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports exceptions versus ordinary return values. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for exceptions versus ordinary return values using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Avoiding exceptions for normal branching), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain exceptions versus ordinary return values, identify its place in exceptions, debugging, and diagnostics, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
